newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia sees inflation fall, faster privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Latvia sees inflation fall, faster privatisation.

text.p: Latvia's economy ministry on Tuesday forecast a continued fall in inflation in 1997 and said that privatisation would be the quickest ever this year.

"We can expect a continued fall of inflation (in the coming years)," economy ministry parliamentary vice-secretary Juris Cebulis told a news conference as he presented a report on Latvia's economy, drawn up by the ministry.
The report forecast that inflation would fall to ten percent this year from an estimated 15.9 percent in 1996.
Latvia showed the lowest inflation compared with fellow Baltic states Estonia and Lithuania in 1994 and 1995.
But Lithuanian 1996 inflation seems likely to be the lowest of the Baltic states as it came in at just 13.1 percent.
The report said that inflation was currently being caused by prices adjusting to world levels as Latvia moved to a fully-developed market economy sytem.
The report said that fuel excise rises and electricity tariffs were the main causes of price rises in 1996, responsible for some three and 2.5 percent of the CPI rise respectively.
The adoption of a balanced 1997 budget is also expected to reduce inflationary pressures.
"Privatisation should continue and according to both our plans and forecasts, the pace of privatisation (in 1997) will be the highest ever," Cebulis said.
He noted that there have been improvements in the terms of privatisations by allowing foreigners to buy land, a bankruptcy law was in place and that laws on foreign investment had been liberalised.

The government of Prime Minister Andris Shkele has set as one of its main aims the privatisation of key state companies such as the oil terminal Ventspils Nafta, electricity firm Latvenergo, gas firm Latvian Gas and the Latvian Shipping Co.
